data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues that 'The complete evidence requirement for distinguishing truly independent failures from cryptic common-cause failures is the monitoring of the independent-causal-pathway supply chains.' But statistical independence tests can also provide distinguishing evidence: the problem asks to 'Identify what evidence would distinguish failure modes that are truly independent from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found.' A shared common-cause failure typically produces a statistically detectable spike in correlated failures during perturbation events. SRC_001's claim of completeness incorrectly excludes statistical/observational evidence as a partial distinguishing mechanism, demanding absolute supply-chain attestation instead.
